claim_a_text: Anchor boxes are an effective and necessary design for efficient region proposal and object detection.
claim_b_text: Anchor boxes have significant drawbacks and can be eliminated in favor of a keypoint-based detection approach.
claim_a_quote: We introduce novel Region Proposal Networks (RPNs) that share convolutional layers with state-of-the-art object detection networks [1], [2]. By sharing convolutions at test-time, the marginal cost for computing proposals is small (e.g., 10ms per image).
claim_b_quote: But the use of anchor boxes has two drawbacks. First, we typically need a very large set of anchor boxes... this creates a huge imbalance between positive and negative anchor boxes and slows down training.
rationale: Article A advocates for anchor boxes as an efficient and effective solution for region proposal, while Article B argues that anchor boxes are problematic due to imbalance and hyperparameter complexity, proposing a different paradigm without anchors.
